data.translation: Gott wollte es so: als ihre neun Monate um waren, bekam Aḥmad Agha einem Sohn und Ḥasan Agha eine Tochter.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (62/8)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr me d hawile l Aḥmad Aġa u abrano, kamilo i šatayḏe, l aloho hawxa ṣbele mayəṯ. Aḥmad Aġa, fayəš u abrayḏe yatumo.
data.translation: Ein Jahr, nachdem Aḥmad Agha diesen Sohn bekommen hatte, wollte Gott es so: Aḥmad Agha starb und sein Sohn wurde Waisenkind.

rationale: Fills Preterit 1 with an overt following death event, showing the content is not limited to favorable outcomes.

summary: The corpus adds a Preterit box for the entry's already printed base ṣbele, not a new stem or lexical sense. All attestations fit I.1 wollen.

Ritter Preterit has l-marked Aloho beside -le, while JTM3.2/30 prints zero-marked Aloho. Infectum has zero-marked Aloho, with bare ṣobe in conditions and kṣobe in 115/239. Do not transfer ʔbʕ argument coding to this root.
The content of willing is often hawxa plus a following outcome, or is recovered from the main clause. ənkan l aloho ṣbele (64/239) is prospective despite the Preterit form.

Lookup verifies zby has the same etymology and the 62/7 birth passage in zbele spelling. This is a spelling/entry overlap, so the new-box claim is limited to ṣby; no normalization or cross-entry merger is silently performed.
Should ṣby and zby be linked or consolidated as spelling variants? zby already contains the parallel 62/7 Preterit quotation.
Does ġalabe in 15/5 modify ṣobe or the following satisfaction predicate? That token is analysed but not selected as an example.
Is the contrast between zero-marked Aloho at JTM3.2/30 and l-marked Aloho in Ritter systematic, dialectal, or editorial?
